item.title: Minor exclusion and planar rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2610.12576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph which is quasi-isometric to a graph excluding a countable clique as a minor is quasi-isometric to a planar graph. Consequently, every finitely generated group with such a quasi-isometry is virtually planar, meaning that some finite-index subgroup admits a planar Cayley graph. We also show that a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph admitting a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding some finite minor admits a regular map into a bounded-degree planar graph. If the source is accessible, the target need only exclude a countable clique. Combined with work of Mackay, Spriano, and the present author, this shows that a finitely presented group admits a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding a countable clique if and only if it is virtually planar.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Paul MacManus

item.title: LInearity of Tubular Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a tubular group is linear if and only if it is residually finite, equivalently virtually primitive. Every such group embeds in $\SL_n(\Z[u])$. For a primitive tubular decomposition with at most $m$ edge slopes at each vertex, our representation has dimension $2\max\{2,m\}$. In particular, Gersten's group embeds in $\SL_6(\Z[u])$, and this dimension is minimal.
item.dc:creator: Daniel T. Wise

item.title: Quasipositive Braids, Presentations, and Garside Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.12808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a presentation of the braid group in which the generating set is the set of all positive half-twists, the relations are balanced positive relations, and every relation is conjugate to one in a finite list. We then prove that for any such presentation, its positive monoid is not isomorphic to the quasipositive braid monoid. Finally, we show that the quasipositive braid monoid has no proper Garside family. These results settle a problem of Calegari from the K3 problems list.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Guynee

item.title: On the number of conjugacy classes of finite solvable groups of order divisible by $p^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.12962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2003, H\'ethelyi and K\"ulshammer proved that if $G$ is a finite solvable group and $p$ is a prime such that $p^2$ divides $|G|$, then $k(G)\geq (49p+1)/60$, and they constructed an infinite family of groups for which this bound was claimed to be attained. We point out that the groups in this family are not Frobenius groups, so that their class numbers are considerably larger than stated, and that in fact the bound is never attained. We then determine the best possible bound of this shape: we show that $k(G)\geq (49p+7)/60$ for all primes $p$, which is sharp for $p=17$, and that $k(G)\geq (49p+451)/60$ for all primes $p>2719$, which is sharp for infinitely many primes $p$. Thus the slope $49/60$ found by H\'ethelyi and K\"ulshammer is best possible, but the correct additive constant is $451/60$ rather than $1/60$.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Michael Keller

item.title: Cohomology and multiplicative gaps for quasi-isometries of nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct two word metrics on the same seven-dimensional torsion-free nilpotent lattice whose asymptotic cones are isometric, but for which every quasi-isometry has multiplicative constant at least $1+\varepsilon$, for one fixed $\varepsilon>0$. We use a convex invariant of a fixed quasi-isometry $\Psi:N\to M$. The displacement cocycle of $\Psi$ and the right-invariant means on $N$ determine a compact convex set $\mathcal A(\Psi)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(V_N,V_M)$. If $\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi)$ denotes the first-layer maps of the graded homomorphisms that occur as blow-downs of $\Psi$ with varying basepoints, then $$ \mathcal A(\Psi)=\operatorname{conv}\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi), \qquad\operatorname{Ext}\mathcal A(\Psi)\subseteq\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi). $$ For every extreme point $L\in\mathcal A(\Psi)$, the dual map $L^*$ is also the degree-one part of an isomorphism of the full real cohomology rings. This cohomological compatibility, together with the realization of first-layer Pansu differentials by invariant means, yields the multiplicative constant gap stated above.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Soumyadeb Samanta, Soumyadip Thandar

item.title: Classes of Subgroups of a finite group with isomorphic quotient groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the poset QIso(G) of classes of subgroups of finite group G having isomorphic quotients. Particularly, we study it for finite abelian groups and for some classes of non-abelian metacyclic groups namely, dihedral groups Dn, the group U2np and affine groups Aff(F) over finite field F. In the case of abelian groups G, we show that QIso(G) and Iso(G) are isomorphic. We show that cyclic groups are the only groups for which QIso(G) is isomorphic to its subgroup lattice. We also show that cyclic groups are the only nilpotent groups for which QIso(G) and its lattice of normal subgroups are isomorphic. We characterize finite 2-groups all of whose subgroups are q-self dual with QIso(G) being a chain. We also characterize all p-groups G of order at most p4 whose QIso(G) is a chain.
item.dc:creator: Tushar Halder, Sachin Ballal

item.title: On $p$-groups with one nonlinear codegree
item.description: arXiv:2610.13371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an irreducible character $\chi$ of a finite group $G$, its codegree is defined by $cod(\chi)=|G:\ker\chi|/\chi(1)$. In this paper, we characterize fnite $p$-groups whose nonlinear irreducible characters all have the same codegree.
item.dc:creator: Jiwei Zheng, Heng Lv

item.title: $D^L$, $D^Q$ Spectrum and Eigenvalue-free Interval of Cayley Graphs over Finite Nilpotent Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite group $G$ and a symmetric connection set $S$, we study the distance Laplacian ($D^L$) and distance signless Laplacian ($D^Q$) spectrum of the Cayley graph $\Cay(G,S)$ for $G$ a finite nilpotent group. Using the internal direct product decomposition over Sylow subgroups, we reduce every question to a single (possibly non-abelian) prime-power factor. In this setting, the required tools are furnished by ordinary representation theory rather than character theory. Based on this framework, we then derive a complete and explicit formula for every eigenvalue, with multiplicity, of the distance matrix, distance Laplacian, and distance signless Laplacian of $\Cay(G,S)$ for $G$ nilpotent: each eigenvalue is indexed by a tuple of irreducible characters of the Sylow factors. Finally, we use the explicit spectrum, together with Perron--Frobenius theory, to determine the eigenvalue-free interval of $D^L$ and $D^Q$.
item.dc:creator: Pallabi Manna, Santanu Mandal

item.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Artin and Coxeter groups whose outer automorphisms are length-preserving
item.description: arXiv:2610.13904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every length-preserving automorphism of a nonspherical Artin or Coxeter group has infinite Reidemeister number. As a consequence, we establish property $R_\infty$ for large-type free-of-infinity Artin groups, infinite strongly rigid Coxeter groups, and infinite virtually abelian Coxeter groups, including all affine Coxeter groups. We also prove that the automorphism group of every infinite irreducible non-affine strongly rigid Coxeter group is acylindrically hyperbolic.
item.dc:creator: Ignat Soroko

item.title: The finite basis problem for varieties generated by all semirings of a fixed order
item.description: arXiv:2610.12486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Avar_n$ and $\VV_n$ be the varieties generated by all $n$-element additively idempotent semirings (ai-semirings) and all $n$-element semirings with commutative addition, respectively, in the signature $(+,\cdot)$ without constants. We prove that both varieties are finitely based if and only if $n\leq2$. The five-element case follows from cyclic identities and a structural analysis of products of squares. For $n\geq6$, each variety contains a finite inherently nonfinitely based ai-semiring. We also prove $\VV_n\cap\AI=\Avar_n$ for every $n$, where $\AI$ is the variety of all ai-semirings.
item.dc:creator: Aifa Wang, Lili Wang

item.title: The six-element additively idempotent semiring $B_2^1$ is inherently nonfinitely based
item.description: arXiv:2610.12491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the six-element additively idempotent semiring $B_2^1$ is inherently nonfinitely based. More precisely, for every positive integer $n$, we construct an infinite additively idempotent semiring, generated by at most $(6n+8)^2$ elements, that satisfies every $n$-variable identity of $B_2^1$.
item.dc:creator: Miao Miao Ren, Meng Ya Yue, Yi Lin Zhou

item.title: Recognizing oriented knots from finite quotients with one marked element
item.description: arXiv:2610.13260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an oriented tame knot $K$, let $G_K$ be its group, with positive meridian $\mu_K$ and preferred longitude $\lambda_K$. We prove that the profinite completion $\widehat{G_K}$, marked by the conjugacy class of $\mu_K\lambda_K$, determines $K$ up to oriented equivalence. In fact, every isomorphism preserving this mark preserves the meridian and longitude with the same conjugator. The proof combines Xu's genuineness theorem with profinite JSJ theory and simultaneous boundary realization, and applies to satellite and composite knots. Consequently, Eisermann's colouring polynomials over all finite groups determine oriented knots.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Biswas, Shrinit Singh

item.title: Actions of Fell bundles, II: tensor products and Fourier-Stieltjes algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.13646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the context of Fell bundles over discrete groups, we introduce and analyze suitable notions of direct sum and tensor product of actions of Fell bundles on Hilbert bundles. For $C^*$-dynamical systems, where actions arise from equivariant representations, we discuss how the tensor product of two such actions is related to the action associated with the tensor product of the underlying equivariant representations. Likewise, since any action gives rise to a $C^*$-correspondence between the full cross-sectional $C^*$-algebras of the involved Fell bundles, we examine the connection between the $C^*$-correspondence associated with the tensor product of two given actions and the tensor product of the associated $C^*$-correspondences. We also discuss how the tensor product of actions naturally appears in Rieffel-like induction processes. Finally we present related results on the Fourier-Stieltjes and Fourier algebras of a Fell bundle.
item.dc:creator: Erik B\'edos, Roberto Conti

item.title: Linearity of Graph Manifold Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We complete the proof that every compact 3-manifold group is linear. Specifically, we construct a faithful representation in GL5(Q[u]) for a finite-index subgroup of every closed non-geometric graph-manifold group.
item.dc:creator: Daniel T. Wise

item.title: Two-orbit right-angled Polytopes and Hypertopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Abstract polytopes and hypertopes are thin and residually-connected incidence geometries or, equivalently, chamber systems. Their degree of regularity is understood by looking at the action of their automorphism group on the set of their chambers. When this action has only one orbit, they are called regular. In this article, we are interested in polytopes and hypertopes with exactly two orbits on their chambers. Let $I = \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For any $J\subsetneq I$ with $|I| \geq 3$, we show that there exists a class $2_J$ two-orbit hypertope whose diagram is any graph on $|I|$ vertices, with edges all labeled by $\infty$. In order to do so, we first establish a general framework for constructing hypertopes as quotient of chamber systems, and then exploit the machinery of acylindrically hyperbolic groups for showing that this framework can be used to create two-orbit polytopes and hypertopes of class $2_J$. Note that all polytopes and hypertopes constructed in this paper are infinite.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Alexandre Piedade, Philippe Tranchida

item.title: Algebro-Geometric Invariants of Finitely Generated Groups (The Profile of a Representation Variety)
item.description: arXiv:0804.0460v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: If G is a finitely generated group, and A an algebraic group, then Hom(G,A) is a possibly reducible algebraic variety denoted by R_A(G). Here we define the profile function, P_d(R_A(G)), of the representation variety of G over A to be P_d(R_A(G))=(N_d(R_A(G)),...,N_0(R_A(G))), where N_i(R_A(G)) stands for the number of irreducible components of R_A(G) of dimension i, where 0\leq i\leq d, and d=Dim(R_A(G)). We then use this invariant in the study of fg groups and prove various results. In particular, we show that if G an orientable surface group of genus g\geq 1, then P_d(R_{SL(2,C)}(G))\neq P_d(R_{PSL(2,C)}(G)). We also show that the same holds for G a torus knot group with presentation <x,y;x^p=y^t> where both p,t are greater than 2, and that the same also holds when G is a the fundamental group of a compact non-orientable surface of genus g\geq 3. Further, we show that if a group G can be n+1 generated, and presented by <x_1,...,x_n,y ; W=y^p>, where W is a non-trivial word in F_n=<x_1,...,x_n>, and A=PSL(2, C), that then Dim(R_{A}(G)) is equal to Max{3n, Dim(R_{A}(G'))+2 \} \leq 3n+1, where G'=<x_1,...,x_n; W=1>. We also give a condition guaranteeing that the resulting algebraic variety is reducible.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano S. Majewicz

item.title: Non-bi-orderable one-relator groups without generalized torsion
item.description: arXiv:2303.07499v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct examples of non-bi-orderable one-relator groups without generalized torsion. This answers a question asked in [2].
item.dc:creator: Azer Akhmedov, James Thorne

item.title: PySymmetry: A Sage/Python Framework for the Symmetry Reduction of Linear G-Equivariant Systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.19479v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite the prevalence of symmetry in scientific linear systems, these structural properties are often underutilized by standard computational software. This paper introduces PySymmetry, an open-source Sage/Python framework that implements classical representation theory to simplify G-equivariant linear systems. PySymmetry uses projection operators to generate symmetry-adapted bases, transforming equivariant operators into a more efficient block-diagonal form. Its functionalities include defining and reducing representations, calculating multiplicities, and obtaining the explicit block structure. We demonstrate PySymmetry's versatility through three case studies: a chemistry application, a numerical benchmark on the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation that achieved a performance increase of over 17x compared to standard methods, and a symbolic investigation that enabled the first complete analytical classification of a challenging problem in celestial mechanics. Designed for seamless integration with libraries like NumPy and SciPy, PySymmetry offers a powerful, user-friendly tool for exploring symmetries in theoretical and applied contexts. ```
item.dc:creator: Leon D. da Silva, Marcelo P. Santos

item.title: Exact versus monotone isoperimetric profiles of finitely generated groups
item.description: arXiv:2509.22260v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gromov asked whether the exact isoperimetric profile of an infinite finitely generated group is comparable, at the same cardinality, to its greatest nondecreasing minorant. We compare finite sets with their translates and construct orders for which the first $r$ vertices have boundary bounded by a fixed multiple of that of the whole set. Such orders follow from profile summability or from rays in Schreier graphs with a uniform bound on the number using each edge. Among infinite finitely generated groups, we obtain comparison and nested exhaustions for elementary amenable and branch groups, direct products of at least two infinite groups, restricted wreath products with two nontrivial factors, and certain simple topological full groups, including amenable derived groups of interval exchanges. The exhausting $n$-point sets have boundary comparable to the monotone profile at $n$. The ray condition is quasi-isometry invariant and holds for the Sierpi\'nski-carpet group. For polycyclic groups of exponential growth, we refine Pittet's construction to obtain explicit nested sets with $|F_n|=n$ and $|\partial F_n|\asymp n/\log n$, answering his question with exact rather than comparable cardinalities. We also prove that the normalized $L^1$ profile satisfies $j(v)\le C(v/u)j(u)$ for $1\le u\le v$ on every infinite connected bounded-degree vertex-transitive graph. This yields the separation bound asked for by Gournay--Le Coz and Hume's Dirichlet--Neumann comparison at $p=1$. For groups of exponential growth, the exact-to-monotone comparison ratio is $O(\log\log n)$. We answer the first part of Correia's Question 1.3 positively by proving the required dilation regularity, and the second negatively by constructing elementary amenable examples whose inverse compositions fail this regularity for every choice of equivalent representatives.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee

item.title: Gluing diagrams part 1: A constructive solution for the Higman-Thompson group isomorphism problem
item.description: arXiv:2605.02889v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces gluing diagrams, a combinatorial tool to construct homomorphisms between the shift pseudogroups of directed graphs and thus also their full groups of shifts. We will establish which of these diagrams produce isomorphisms. As an application, using the interpretation of Higman-Thompson groups as full groups of shifts of specific graphs, we will describe a procedure that constructs gluing diagrams that explicitly describe the isomorphisms between Higman-Thompson groups, conjectured by Higman and whose existence was proven by Pardo arXiv:1006.1759. This procedure will follow Euclid's algorithm and will allow us to lift isomorphisms to higher arity.
item.dc:creator: Roman Gorazd

item.title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups of type ${}^2 A_3$ and ${}^2 A_4$ over Local Rings
item.description: arXiv:2609.02617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a complete classification of the automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$, and of their elementary subgroups, over commutative local rings $R$ containing $1/2$ and equipped with a non-trivial involution $\theta$. The classification covers all isogeny types and, together with our higher-rank result~\cite{EB&DM1}, completes the description for type ${}^2A_{\ell}$ with $\ell\geq3$.
item.dc:creator: Elena I. Bunina, Deep H. Makadiya

item.title: Profinite rigidity of K\"ahler groups: Riemann surfaces and subdirect products
item.description: arXiv:2501.13761v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper establishes strong profinite rigidity results for K\"ahler groups, showing that certain groups are determined within the class of residually finite K\"ahler groups by their profinite completion. Examples include products of surface groups and certain groups with exotic finiteness properties studied earlier by Dimca-Papadima-Suciu and Llosa Isenrich. Consequently, there are aspherical smooth projective varieties that are determined up to homeomorphism by their algebraic fundamental group. The main tool is the following: the holomorphic fibrations of a closed K\"ahler manifold over hyperbolic 2-orbifolds can be recovered from the profinite completion of its fundamental group. We also prove profinite invariance of the BNS invariant.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hughes, Claudio Llosa Isenrich, Pierre Py, Matthew Stover, Stefano Vidussi
